Dialogs.Dialog: Anegasaki
Hey, 'Hell's Bon Dance' is airing on TV tonight.
Hell's... what？
Bon Dance. They say it's a cult horror masterpiece. Wanna watch it together？
Tonight, together？ A movie on TV？ I mean... sure...
Then it's a plan.
Wait a sec, whose room？
Our own rooms. I'll text you when the opening starts.
Text... on our phones？
Yep. We'll text our thoughts and screams to each other while we watch. It'll be fun.
So basically... we're doing live commentary？
Ah, 'Hell's Bon Dance'... I can't wait for tonight~
Anegasaki
Oh yeah, 'Hell's Bon Dance' was so scary the other day.
Felt more like a comedy movie to me.
You were scared! You texted me stuff like 'A zombie!' and 'So much blood!'
Well, texting each other while watching the same movie was pretty fun.
So, 'Dracula Samurai: Bat Sword' is on late tonight. Wanna watch it together again？
Just from the title, I get the feeling it's a terrible B-movie...
It's not a B-movie.
...It is, isn't it？
More like C or D... Hmm, maybe a Z-movie.
We're... watching that？
Together.
I've been meaning to ask, why was that sword in 'Dracula Samurai' weak to salt？
Anegasaki
You probably wouldn't get it unless you saw the prequel, 'The Bloodsucking Slug'.
There's a prequel...? Draculas and slugs don't exactly have much in common.
They both suck blood.
I don't think slugs do that.
It's a 'Bloodsucking Slug', so it does. They both love blood. That's what they share.
...I'm not convinced.
Hehe, do you really need to be convinced？
(That's probably the right attitude to have...)
Anegasaki
I bought the DVD for 'The Bloodsucking Slug'. Wanna watch it？ I'll lend it to you.
You bought it？ Or rather, that actually got a DVD release？
I'll bring it to Dexee's.
▲姉ヶ崎＊▲, do you spend your paychecks on DVDs like that？
Of course not. I usually just rent them.
But you bought 'The Bloodsucking Slug'.
Well, you said you hadn't seen it. So I figured... And I wanted to watch it again.
Should we text each other while watching the DVD, too？
If you want to.
If ▲姉ヶ崎＊▲ asks me to, that is.
Acting all spoiled... You're like a little kid.
Anegasaki
Cell phones have so many features these days, I don't think I use them all...
Like, you can watch TV, but I can't exactly do that at school or work.
I wish we could swap out features. Like, 'I don't need this, give me this.'
Like what？
A can opener.
...Is that a 'feature'？
Haven't you ever wanted to open a can of mackerel and couldn't find the opener？
...I guess I have.
See？ Now you're starting to think a phone with a can opener would be handy.
It might be handy, but... would it really be？
Anegasaki
Oh, I just thought of another add-on feature I'd want for my phone.
Besides a can opener？
This one is an absolute must-have. People will wonder how they ever lived without it.
I can't even imagine.
A hanko stamp.
...A hanko？ Where would you even put that on a phone？
Haven't you ever panicked when a delivery arrives and you can't find your stamp？
...I guess I have.
See？ Now you're starting to think a phone with a hanko would be handy.
But where would the hanko even go on the phone？
That's up to the maker, but it'd be nice if it tucked away when not in use.
(I mean, sure, but that's not really the issue...)
Anegasaki
Don't you think a phone with a built-in hanko would be a massive hit？
...No, I don't.
Then what kind of feature do you think would be good？
Given the shape of a phone, maybe an electric razor？ Salarymen would love it, so it'd probably be a hit.
Women wouldn't use a feature like that.
A shoehorn might be pretty handy.
I'd be a little hesitant to put something I use on my feet against my face.
What about a Phillips-head screwdriver？
That's another feature women wouldn't really care about, I think.
This is tough.
See, it has to be a hanko.
Anegasaki
Oh yeah, I heard people used to carry cell phones slung over their shoulders.
Over their shoulders？ What do you mean？
Like a shoulder bag. Apparently they weighed around three kilos, too.
Three kilos？ Did they have dumbbells in them or something？
Maybe they really did work like bags. I heard they were sold with things inside.
Huh.
Then you could fit a can opener, a stamp, an electric shaver, a shoehorn, and a Phillips screwdriver in it.
Oh! And a clock, a radio, and a camera must've been in there too. Then they slowly got smaller...
Until they became the size they are today. Hehe.
(No way that's true.)
Anegasaki
Hey, I was just thinking...
What？
We're really close, aren't we？
No, thanks.
We're always together. We even work most of the same shifts at our job.
We're apart during class, though.
Hehe, sadly. But we still commute to and from school together like this.
...Is there a problem with that？
Do you think we look like we're all over each other？
I don't think it's anything to worry about... Did someone say something？
No, it's not that.
Anegasaki
...Should we walk a bit further apart？ We might look too lovey-dovey.
You said something like that before. Did something happen？
J-Son... I watched 'Doomsday J-Son'.
Ah, the one with the masked killer.
J-Son goes after the teens visiting the lake, one by one...
It's fine, we're not at a lake.
But J-Son goes to New York, and even to space! And...
The ones who get targeted first are always the lovey-dovey couples!
Are ● really being that lovey-dovey？
So I thought it might be dangerous if we are.
Lovey-dovey...
Geez, it's dangerous, so stay away!
If it's that J-Son series you mentioned, ● saw a few of them on TV.
Anegasaki
The ones targeted first were the lovey-dovey couples, right？
Lovey-dovey... Or rather, the victims are usually your typical dumb couples.
Dumb couples？ Like what, specifically...？
Well, first, they laugh together a lot.
...That's us.
And they're always together wherever they go.
And they stay in the same tent when they go camping.
I'd be too scared to sleep separately in a place like that. I need you with me.
...Are ● a dumb couple？
We do fit the criteria.
Isn't that fine？ It's fun, at least.
Hmm...
Anegasaki
If J-Son does show up... You're the one I'm worried about.
●？ Why's that？
Because the girls always survive, and the boys get wiped out.
As long as ▲姉ヶ崎＊▲ is safe, it's fine.
No it's not！ You have to survive too.
I don't want ● to die either, but... hey, maybe it's time we watch something else.
Yeah, the 14th one we watched yesterday was the end of the series anyway.
There were that many？ Yeah, watching all of them would definitely mess with your head...
▲主人公＊▲. Promise me you'll always stay safe.
Oh, of course.
I absolutely don't want you to die.
Of course, I won't die, ever！
...That just now felt kind of like a silly couple thing to say, huh.
Anegasaki
You cook for yourself, right？
Not every day, though.
And the rest is from convenience stores？
Mostly convenience stores, I guess... I go to the supermarket sometimes, though.
You don't shop at the shopping district？
Shopping there makes me feel like a housewife. It's kind of embarrassing...
There are lots of great stores there, you know？ Vegetables, fruits, and fish.
Fruits aside, veggies and fish are a pain to cook.
Boiling, grilling, stir-frying. It's easy, you know？
It's not easy... Unless ▲姉ヶ崎＊▲ does it for me.
Hm, what was that？
...Never mind.
Anegasaki
Are you making sure to eat a balanced diet？
I'm fine. It's not just convenience stores. Dexee's gives me meals on the late shift, too.
I know, but I'm worried your diet is unbalanced.
At school, I buy bread at the store. I get coffee milk, too.
And at the convenience store？
Canned mackerel... I buy bentos too, keeping balance in mind.
How do you balance a convenience store bento？
Like, yesterday was a fried chicken bento, so today is tonkatsu. I mix it up like that.
Is there really a difference between fried chicken and tonkatsu？
Yeah, they're totally different. One's a bird, one's a mammal. Chickens and pigs sound different.
Jeez, it's not a laughing matter.
When cooking rice, there's that 'up to your wrist' rule, right？
Anegasaki
The amount of water you add to the washed rice.
Yeah. That kind of vague explanation is no good, right？
...No good？ That's what people have always said.
It's not the old days anymore, so just blindly believing old sayings is no good.
...You cooked for yourself？
Yeah.
...You cooked some rice.
...And you messed it up.
...Yeah.
There, there. Don't cry.
You know that legend about measuring the water for rice up to your wrist？
Anegasaki
Legend？
Or myth, whatever. It's weird. Why does everyone believe it？ It's a total lie.
I don't think it's a lie...
A pro wrestler's hand is twice the size of yours, ●! 'Up to the wrist' is so sloppy!
You use a pretty modern rice cooker, right？
I bought the newest model when I moved. An electronic something-or-other.
You don't need to stick your hand in those. Just fill it to the line and you're set.
You'll get it right next time.
...Yeah.
I'll be fine, I'll be fine.
Anegasaki
You know about glass slippers？
Do I？ Where are they？
In fairy tales. But honestly, there's no way anyone could actually wear them...
Well... Hmm, I wonder.
Imagine shoes made of glass. ...See, they broke. They'd shatter.
They were tempered glass. Like what they use for car windows or skyscrapers.
It was a long time ago. They didn't have that tech.
Hmm. Then what would happen？
The glass shards would leave your feet completely bloody... Ah, how scary.
Is this a horror movie？!
I'm just saying, it's scary when you think about reality.
We talked about glass slippers before, right...？
Anegasaki
The shoes breaking and leaving your feet bloody...
Enough of that already. Maybe the person wearing them was just really light？
Their weight？
Yeah, slim and light enough that wearing glass slippers would be perfectly fine.
So if I wore them, would I end up bloody after all？
Ah, you thought it.
I did not! You could wear them too, ▲姉ヶ崎＊▲. You'd be fine!
Liar. There's no way a person like that exists.
(Well, it was a joke to begin with...)
Anegasaki
You know about invisible people？
Do I？ Where are they？
Hehe, in movies. If you could turn invisible, what would you want to do？
●？ If you turned invisible...
Are you thinking about something weird？
...Not at all？
*Sigh*... I think I need a lie detector more than a way to turn invisible.
You really don't trust me, huh.
Lie detector activated... If you lie, no more kisses for you.
...Maybe just a little.
Hehe, hey now!
Come to think of it, is there anything ▲姉ヶ崎＊▲ would want to do if invisible?
Anegasaki
The invisible man stuff? ...I'd probably practice swimming.
Swimming... Why？
Because practicing swimming at my age is embarrassing.
It'd be pretty suspicious to just see splashes in a pool. You'd stand out even more.
Then I'd do it in an empty pool.
...You wouldn't need to be invisible for that, then.
It'd be bad if someone showed up in the middle of it.
Then ● will be right there with you.
With an invisible person? Are you sure you'd know where I am？
I'd know. There's no way ● would ever lose sight of ▲姉ヶ崎＊▲.
Hehe, you're such a smooth talker.
Anegasaki
They say if you make a wish on a shooting star, it comes true, right？
The one where you have to say it three times, right.
Right, and that's the problem.
Shooting stars are only there for a second, after all.
I practiced tongue twisters when I was little for it.
Yeah, ● did too.
Did it work out？
I wanted a toy, but the product name was too long, so no. What about ▲姉ヶ崎＊▲？
The Kids' Beads Super Pretty Set. Just saying it once was hard enough.
I see...
Hehe, should we practice then？
Come to think of it, have you been practicing your wish for a shooting star？
Anegasaki
▲姉ヶ崎＊▲ was the one who suggested we practice, right？
Thinking about it... there's nothing I want badly enough to wish for.
Really？ What about clothes or DVDs or something.
If I'm wishing on a star, it has to be a treasure you can't just buy in a store...
A treasure？
Yeah. Plus, I already have that treasure, so I'm good.
What kind of treasure is it？
...This.
Anegasaki
Sometimes when I remember it... my heart starts pounding.
What？
When I... confessed my feelings to you.
● was just happy about it, though.
Jeez, and here I felt like I was jumping off the stage at Kiyomizu.
The stage at Kiyomizu...
What's wrong？
You know, the stage at Kiyomizu isn't actually all that high in person.
So my pounding heart wasn't that big of a deal, then？
No, no! That's not what I meant at all.
It is high. Super high. Like, 100 kilometers high.
(...100 kilometers？)
Anegasaki
Oh yeah, I heard the stage is only about 11 meters.
...Wait, wasn't it 100 kilometers？
Jeez, you're mean!
Haha, sorry. At 11 meters, an action star could probably jump off it.
A normal person couldn't. Maybe it'd be a little safer if you laid out some mats.
Then maybe even ● could get away with just a broken bone or a sprain.
Not just mats, you'd need a rescue chute like they use in evacuation drills...
Or I could just use a ladder.
A ladder is scary too. Tie a rope around your waist, and then...
Uh... I don't actually have to jump off it, right？
Hmm... it'd be pretty cool if you yelled 'I love you!' while jumping, wouldn't it？
(...Would it really？)
